methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Fairfax City Business Leaders Tell Spanberger About Rising Costs, AI, Workforce Challenges - Patch
signals.signal_reading: Fairfax business leaders discussing AI with Congressional representatives signals deep engagement with emerging technology at the policy level, but the metro-concentrated nature of this dialogue reinforces NoVA's capability advantages over regions lacking similar access to federal power brokers.

signals.title: Virginia Beach schools bring ChatGPT under division oversight as AI use grows - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach schools bringing ChatGPT under division oversight represents distributed but shallow AI adoption—platform tools spreading broadly through institutions without necessarily building deep technical capability or AI literacy among users.

signals.title: Norfolk looks to add AI dispatcher tool for non-emergency calls - WAVY.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk deploying an AI dispatcher for non-emergency calls exemplifies shallow-but-distributed adoption: municipalities purchasing turnkey AI solutions that improve efficiency without developing internal AI expertise or capability to build custom systems.

signals.title: How one Virginia county’s AI platform protects sensitive data - route-fifty.com
signals.signal_reading: A Virginia county building its own AI platform with data protection capabilities signals deep, locally-developed technical capacity rather than vendor dependence—exactly the distributed expertise pattern that distinguishes 'Build It Yourself' from platform-driven adoption.

signals.title: Virginia Tech sets course for human-centered AI leadership - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech positioning for human-centered AI leadership concentrates advanced research capability in the New River Valley, creating a potential secondary hub but also reinforcing the pattern where deep AI expertise clusters around major research universities rather than distributing statewide.
